title: QuantiFERON blood test for TB
what: This is a blood test from a vein. It shows if your body has met the germ that causes tuberculosis.
why: Instead of or together with a TB skin test, before some treatments, after contact with someone with TB, or for work or school.
duration: the blood draw takes 3 to 5 minutes; results usually come in 2 to 7 days
tell_doctor: If you take steroids or medicines that weaken the immune system
If you have HIV or another condition that weakens immunity
If you were in contact with someone with TB
Results of any past TB skin tests (Mantoux or Diaskintest)

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually fasting, or a few hours after a light meal. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Wear a sleeve that is easy to roll up above the elbow.

bring: Past TB test results, if you have them
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
Blood is drawn into several special tubes
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
Results usually come in 2 to 7 days
A positive result does not mean you are ill. A TB specialist will decide what is next

faq.q: Why is this test better than a skin test?
faq.a: It is not affected by the BCG vaccine, and you do not need to come back to have your arm checked.

faq.q: If the test is positive, am I contagious?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The test shows contact with the germ. Other tests show whether it is active disease.

reminders.text: TB blood test tomorrow. Check if you need to come fasting.
